summary.headline: A tax-collecting monopoly with superb returns, but profit has stalled
summary.text: Distilleries Company of Sri Lanka (DIST.N0000), 92% owned by Melstacorp, is the country's dominant arrack maker (and now also brews beer through DCSL Breweries Lanka). It is extremely profitable: return on equity 77%, no debt, Rs 5.7bn of net cash, and about 80% of profit paid out (Rs 3.00 a share for 2025/26). But profit has stopped growing because the government takes most of the price: excise duty was Rs 102.9bn of Rs 164.4bn gross turnover in 2025/26, and a higher income-tax rate for alcohol makers cut profit 4% that year; April–June 2026 profit fell another 7% (EPS Rs 0.86 against Rs 0.92). At Rs 58.00 (CSE, 12 November 2026) it trades at 15.9x trailing earnings with a 5.2% yield. Four methods put fair value at about Rs 32.70, so the price is about 77% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 27.80 and treat under Rs 24.50 as a strong buy. Only 7.65% of the shares are publicly held.

highlights.title: April–June 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Gross revenue up 12% to Rs 41.6bn and net revenue up 14% to Rs 14.5bn, but cost of sales rose 53%, so gross profit fell 6%. Profit fell 7% to Rs 3.96bn (EPS Rs 0.86 against Rs 0.92); tax took 45% of pre-tax profit.

highlights.title: 2025/26 (audited)
highlights.text: Gross turnover Rs 164.4bn (up 18%), of which excise duty Rs 102.9bn. Profit after tax Rs 16.8bn (company), down 4%, after a higher income-tax rate for the alcohol industry. Group EPS Rs 3.71; dividend Rs 3.00 (82% payout).

highlights.title: Into beer
highlights.text: DCSL Breweries Lanka is being integrated into the group, adding beer to the arrack and spirits portfolio.

highlights.title: Very small free float
highlights.text: Melstacorp owns 92.35%; the public holds 7.65%, so trading can be thin.

higher: Excise or income-tax relief for legal producers.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2024/25 and 2025/26 annual reports and the interim reports to June 2026 (unaudited). The September 2026 quarter wasn't in the folder. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: about 77% above fair value of Rs 32.70.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 58: About -8% a year: dividend 5.2% + growth about 4% − about 17% a year if the price moved to fair value.
Decision box.Confidence: Medium: the business is stable, but tax policy can change profit quickly.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Buy 15% below fair value (Rs 27.80), strong buy 25% below (Rs 24.50).

Business and moat.What it does: Arrack (coconut and blended), other spirits and, since the breweries acquisition, beer through DCSL Breweries Lanka.
Business and moat.Moat: Very wide: market leader for decades, brand recall, licences and scale; the main competitor is illicit alcohol.

Sri Lanka checks.Taxes: High risk: excise duty and a higher income-tax rate for alcohol.
Sri Lanka checks.Illicit alcohol: Risk: grows when legal prices rise.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: A near-monopoly with huge returns and cash payouts, at a lower price.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 42.51); a large tax increase.
